root_cause.text: The `rxrpc_input_packet_on_conn` function in the RXRPC subsystem unconditionally calls `rxrpc_put_call` in the implicit-end error path without verifying that a valid call reference was acquired, causing a kernel crash when processing packets after the associated call object has been torn down.
root_cause.evidence: The patch modifies `net/rxrpc/io_thread.c` to conditionally execute `rxrpc_put_call` only if `call` is not NULL, addressing the CVE description which states the error path "unconditionally calls rxrpc_put_call()" even when `rxrpc_try_get_call()` returns NULL because `chan->call` is NULL.

vuln_statements.explanation: Based on the vulnerability root cause, the rxrpc_input_packet_on_conn function in net/rxrpc/io_thread.c contains an unconditional rxrpc_put_call() call in the implicit-end error path. This statement lacks verification that a valid call reference was acquired before calling put_call, which causes a kernel crash when processing packets after the associated call object has been torn down. The Second Evidence Set confirms this file is involved in the RXRPC input processing path.
